featured_reviews.name: ashok mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Happy experience...
Thanks doctors....

Yes my friends,
People write many nasty experience they face in hospital or with doctors. Very few write their sweet experiences in hospital or with doctors.

So I thought to share my excellent sweet experience with a small, faraway hospital but with exceptional expertise in the field of knee replacement and other orthopedic and neurological complication.

My wife Operated for knee replacement on 15th...At 11 in the morning (to 2.30 pm) including recovery time inside operation theatre...

Then shifted to ICU.
Operation was good, my wife was in jolly mood and smiling while coming out from OT after the replacement ... But after 2 hrs of shifting to ICU, the real pain started... Wife was crying like mad for pain... But through medication by 8 pm it has started reducing... and she slept.
Nxt day, 16th, morning no pain...and shifted to pvt room cabin. I also staying in the same room with her. Excellent clean cosy room with all necessary requirements like AC, TV, eye catching view from 4th floor Window, attached very clean bath (no balcony), clean and daily fresh linen.

17th.. Sr Doctors and physiotherapist started her to walk and bent the new knee to 90°...

This was regular exercise, bending knee to 90° and walking in the corridor with the help of walker and physiotherapist till 19th...

And on 19th all bandage and all drain-pipes ( 3 in total... For Blood to drain our excess blood at operated knee, one for urine, one at spinal joint to push different medicine ) removed and....
discharged in the afternoon by doctor...
Same day, 19th, came to home by evening.

She is recovering nicely.... Walking inside the flat with the help of walker... pain she feel very very rarely.

After 9th day from operation, today (24th March) was the first check up...and it is absolutely OK.
Infact, my wife walk through out the day in hospital alone with the help of walker.
Today, she has been allowed by doctor to move and do morning/evening walk with walker and asked for further check up after 15 days.
No medicine given except multivitamin for further recovery as she has no pain.

We are very very happy for the excellent smooth operation, expertise of doctors, quick recovery process with effective treatment, support of Jr. Doctors, Physiotherapist, Metron, Sisters, Brothers, room boy and aayas for 24×7 and overall management of the hospital.

Well behaved people....
No extra billing...

We, and no one, before surgery, expected that after operation on 2nd day pain would vanish... she would walk and bend knee to 90°and get discharge on 4th day...!!!

All credit goes to Dr. Rahul Bade and his team including Anesthesists Dr. Ganesh Kolhe at Sparsh Multi-Speciality Hospital.

Thank you...well done, doctor !!!
🙏🙏🙏

Thanks to Lt. Col Dr Amogh Yadav from Mumbai and Dr. Rahul Mane for strongly recomanding us the hospital.

(Note : Treatment was going on at Sanchiti Hospital. But operated at Sparsh Multi Speciality Hospital)

owner_posts.post_text: In a world that moves fast, yoga reminds us to slow down, breathe, and reconnect with ourselves.

A patient came to us after nearly three months of continuous fever following a knee replacement surgery. During this period, she had consulted multiple doctors across cities and was treated for common infections like typhoid, malaria and dengue. Despite repeated tests and treatments, the fever persisted, along with joint pain, mouth ulcers and extreme fatigue — without a clear diagnosis.

At SRV Hospitals, under the care of Dr. Avilash Tiwari @dr.avilash_tiwari, the approach shifted from treating symptoms to understanding the full cause. A structured evaluation for long-standing fever was initiated, looking beyond routine infections and considering inflammatory and immune-related conditions.

Advanced testing revealed two key findings. One was a mild, uncommon form of leptospirosis that does not present with the typical severe symptoms and often goes unnoticed. More importantly, investigations confirmed an autoimmune condition called Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), where the immune system becomes overactive and causes ongoing inflammation — leading to persistent fever and joint symptoms.

1) We were told Bed Available in ICU on 28th September 2016 & we got him to your hospital. Apparently it was Emergency & to our surprise, he was kept on a Trolley (Stretcher) for the whole night. There was no Monitor attached & your Doctors Prescribed me to buy CHEST LEADS. (I have photograph of the same). The bed was given on 29th September 2016 in the afternoon.As a policy we know you will be charging me a full charge for ICU & there will be definitely no choice left for me but to pay.

2) Basic Hygiene: There is no Blanket in ICU. I was surprised. Your hospital gives a worn out Solapuri Bed Sheet to cover. The clothes given are soild, the pillow cover is drenched in Oil & dirty.

3) CARE in ICU: Yesterday at night I just came in to see how my father is doing. He has to have a BIPAP machine put on for whole night due to his saturation issue. To my utter surprise, the BIPAP machine was not put on properly, the oxygen flow pipe was not attached. When I asked my father who put this, he said a ward boy came & put it. So do I understand that such critical things are handled by Ward Boys in your ICU & not by an RMO or Nurse. The saturation had dipped to 75 & I had to call the RMO on duty.

3) Payments: I remember we had spoken last time of unavailability of Credit Card in Zen & you assured me that its rectified & working. To my utter surprise a big hospital like JOY, the credit card swipping machine is not working & no one is bothered. Later on i was told that you charge 1.43% transaction fee and hospital prefers cash collection this was told by your billing team. Or the feeling I get is that the hospital encourages CASH payments. Also no hospital in Mumbai including a hospital like Shushrut in Chembur which is run by a trust charges a transaction fee for any credit card swipe. I am informed that your hospital does charge a transaction fee. Do we ever ask your team what is the base cost of doing Hgt or giving 1 round of nebulization. The machine cost 2500 and you charge 100 per nebulization and medicine we only have to buy.

Dr. Patankar - I have nothing against you personally, nor against your organisation JOY Hospital. Infact its a boon for us that you exist next door for any emergency. But such things which happen puts one off & then prompts to make a noise about it. Your ICU bed charges & other charges are in line with any of the High profile hospitals in Mumbai. But others at least take care of the patients & treat it on a more humanitarian & compassionate way.

Today Social Media is very active, a Single Tweet or a Facebook post is enough for such things to go Viral on the Social Media. I can also understand that last time my comments on Facebook must have irked you as the set up was new, but those were never a complaint but a guideline for your organisation to improve.

This is a feedback on the services provided by an organisation where you are a Director. Such things can bring a disrepute to an organisation & seriously tarnish the image. I have noticed one thing which I want to share freely is that people have no choice when Emergency hit them & are dependent on medical care. We know its an organisation you are running & there is a cost attached to it but what we expect is CARE with Compassion & not just a source to make revenue on someones emergency situation.
